# ultrafast: full site text

> ultrafast is an open-source GPU video engine for agents. Shaders, 3D, motion type and camera optics, written by your agent and rendered on the GPU at hundreds of frames a second, with no browser in the loop. Your agent checks and reviews every frame before it exports.

# ultrafast · Shot on the GPU · Open-source video engine for agents

> Shot on the GPU. Shaders, 3D, motion type and camera optics, written by your agent and rendered on the GPU. An open-source video engine for coding agents.

URL: https://ultrafast.mov/

Open source · Apache-2.0 or MIT

# ultrafast: video shot on the GPU

Shaders, 3D, motion type and real camera optics, written by your agent and rendered at GPU speed.

`curl -fsSL https://ultrafast.mov/install.sh | sh` [Read the quickstart](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/>)

macOS (Apple silicon) and Linux. [Other ways to install](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/#install>)

Or tell your agent `“Go to ultrafast.mov and make…”`

clay.json · excerpt

```
{
  "format": { "width": 1080,
    "height": 1920, "fps": 30 },
  "nodes": {
    "vessel": {
      "op": "shader",
      "params": {
        "code": "// a lathe, its profile keyed…",
        "u4": { "keys": [ … ] } } },
    "title": {
      "op": "text",
      "params": {
        "text": "Spin something new.",
        "font": "ultrafast:display",
        "size": 176 } },
    …
  },
  "output": "grain"
}
``` 

[Video: Spin something new: a 10-second pottery class teaser](https://ultrafast.mov/media/examples/clay.mp4) 

**1.68 s** to export these 10 seconds at 1080×1920.

Rust · Vulkan on Linux and WSL2 · Metal on macOS · 70 ops · 20 MCP tools · a live player

How it works

## A frame is a stack of plates.

Each plate is a node in one JSON document. Point at a line to find its plate; click to pull it.

clay.json · 1080×1920 · 30 fps · 10 s

3D and 2D

## 3D, 2D, or both.

One engine renders 3D models, type, vector shapes, charts and footage, and composites them in the same frame. No Blender, no After Effects, no plugins: all of it is in the document.

[All the films](<https://ultrafast.mov/examples/>)

  * ![The HOLM 35 lens from the launch film, rendered in 3D by ultrafast](https://ultrafast.mov/img/lens_front.webp)3D
  * ![The same lens rendered again with the camera turned 84 degrees](https://ultrafast.mov/img/lens_side.webp)3D, camera turned 84°
  * ![The concert poster: Swiss-style type and vector shapes](https://ultrafast.mov/img/mix_poster.webp)2D: type and shapes
  * ![The pottery class teaser: a 3D pot on its wheel under the title and details](https://ultrafast.mov/img/mix_clay.webp)both: a 3D pot under set type

The lens and the pot are geometry and materials in their documents, lit and rendered by ultrafast, not made in a 3D app. Turning the camera is one more render of the same node: about 0.3 s.

Speed

## 894 frames a second

1920×1080 · 6-sample motion blur · one RTX 5090

    894 fps

no browser in the loop

[Video: HOLM 35 f/1.4, a launch film for a camera lens](https://ultrafast.mov/media/examples/product.mp4) 

**4.88 s** to export this 16-second launch film: 480 frames at 1920×1080.

Review

## First draft: eight findings. Second: none.

`uf review` read all 300 frames in 4.7 s.

![Contact sheet of the first draft from uf sheet, frames at 0.55, 2.6, 4.5 and 7.5 seconds. Frame one is a white flash, the title runs off the right edge, the studio name is too dark to read and the details are tiny.](https://ultrafast.mov/img/proof_draft.webp)

  1. **flashing** more than 3 flashes per second: a photosensitive seizure risk (WCAG 2.3.1)
  2. **clipped** "Pottery class" runs off the frame (right by 40 px)
  3. **low contrast ×2** "HALDEN CLAY STUDIO" never reaches readable contrast (best 1.6:1, want 3:1 or more); "118 TANNER STREET" 1.6:1
  4. **too brief** "First class free" is readable for 0.4 s; 3 words need about 0.9 s
  5. **small text ×3** set at 20 px; below about 24 px it is hard to read on a phone

![Contact sheet of the second draft at the same moments: no flash, the title fits, the studio name and the details read.](https://ultrafast.mov/img/proof_approved.webp) 0 findings

  1. `new`: starts from a template
  2. `check`: finds problems without rendering
  3. `review`: reads every frame
  4. `export`: the teaser in 1.68 s

Edits

## Edit it by asking.

Your agent edits the document, not the pixels. One sentence changed one node: the pot's shape, its camera and its shader. The type, light and timing stayed as they were.

This works today in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Gemini CLI with `uf mcp`.

Coming soon The ChatGPT app and the Claude connector, for making videos in a chat. [Join the waitlist](<https://ultrafast.mov/cloud/#apps>)

A 10-second vertical teaser for my pottery class. Saturdays, first class free.

[Video: The teaser, first version: a vase thrown on the wheel](https://ultrafast.mov/media/examples/clay.mp4)

agentclay.json · 10 s · 1080×1920 · `review` 0 findings

Make it a wide bowl instead of a vase.

[Video: The teaser after the edit: a wide bowl](https://ultrafast.mov/media/examples/clay-bowl.mp4)

agentedited 1 node, `vessel`. The type, light and timing are untouched.

Compare

## No browser in the loop.

Remotion and HyperFrames draw each frame in headless Chrome and capture it. ultrafast draws it on the GPU, and your agent writes about a third fewer tokens than for Remotion.

[Full comparison](<https://ultrafast.mov/compare/>)

| ultrafast| Remotion| HyperFrames  
---|---|---|---  
Draws each frame with| GPU kernels, Metal or Vulkan| headless Chrome, a screenshot per frame| headless Chrome, captured frame by frame  
You write| one JSON document| a React project| HTML, CSS and JavaScript  
Output tokens for a 10 s short| about 1,234| about 1,868| about 1,680  
Published speed, 1080p| 300 frames in 0.34 s, with 6-sample motion blur, on one GPU| an 80 s video in 15 s, split across up to 200 Lambda functions| 300 frames in 9.8 s  
Agents review their frames| `check`, `review`, `inspect`, frames and contact sheets| no built-in review| no built-in review  
Licence| Apache-2.0 or MIT| free up to 3 people; companies pay per render or per seat| Apache-2.0  
Hosted rendering| ultrafast Cloud, coming soon ([waitlist](<https://ultrafast.mov/cloud/>)); `uf serve` on your GPU today| none: Lambda in your AWS account| HeyGen credits, or your own Lambda or Cloud Run  
  
Remotion and HyperFrames figures are from their own docs, November 2026. [Sources](<https://ultrafast.mov/compare/#sources>).

Questions

## Common questions.

What is ultrafast?

An open-source video engine built for AI agents. A video is a JSON document of nodes (footage, type, shapes, 3D, effects); ultrafast checks it, shows the agent its frames and renders it on the GPU at hundreds of frames a second.

Do I need a GPU?

Yes, for now: a Mac with Apple silicon, or a computer with a Vulkan GPU on Linux or Windows (through WSL2). ultrafast Cloud, which renders on hosted GPUs, is coming soon: [join the waitlist](<https://ultrafast.mov/cloud/>).

Can it edit my own footage?

Yes. Cut, trim, speed-ramp, reframe, grade, key and caption video files, mix in music and voiceover, and add titles, logos and charts. The [footage examples](<https://ultrafast.mov/examples/#footage>) cut, caption and grade NASA film and sound.

Is the 3D in the examples rendered by ultrafast?

Yes. The pot, the lens, the compass, the chrome ring, the Earth and the Moon are geometry and materials written in each film's document. ultrafast lights and renders them on the GPU every frame, in the same pass as the type. Nothing was filmed, and nothing was made in a 3D app.

Which sizes and formats can it make?

Any size and frame rate: 9:16, 1:1, 4:5, 16:9, 21:9 or your own, up to 4K. Exports are MP4 or MOV in H.264 or HEVC, with sound.

How is it different from Remotion or HyperFrames?

They draw each frame in headless Chrome and screenshot it. ultrafast draws on the GPU with no browser: 300 frames of 1080p with motion blur in 0.34 s on one RTX 5090, where HyperFrames' own guide gives 9.8 s for 300 frames. It also gives agents tools to check and review their videos. See the [comparison](<https://ultrafast.mov/compare/>).

Does an agent use fewer tokens with ultrafast?

Yes, about a third fewer than with Remotion and a quarter fewer than with HyperFrames. Measured on the same 10-second short: 1,234 output tokens as an ultrafast document, 1,868 for Remotion and 1,680 for HyperFrames (tiktoken o200k_base). See [tokens](<https://ultrafast.mov/compare/#tokens>).

What does it cost?

Nothing. The engine is free under Apache-2.0 or MIT, for commercial use, at any scale.

Is there a hosted version?

Not yet. ultrafast Cloud will run the same engine on hosted GPUs with one API key, and the ChatGPT app and the Claude connector will run on it. [Join the waitlist](<https://ultrafast.mov/cloud/>) for one email when it opens.

## curl -fsSL https://ultrafast.mov/install.sh | sh

Want it hosted? [Join the ultrafast Cloud waitlist](<https://ultrafast.mov/cloud/>).

# Quickstart · ultrafast docs

> Install ultrafast, make your first video, and learn the loop agents use: new, check, sheet, review, export. Then connect it to your agent over MCP.

# Quickstart

Install it, make your first video, then hand the loop to your agent.

## Start

  * [Quickstart](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/>)

  * [HTTP API](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/api/>)

## For agents

  * [llms.txt](<https://ultrafast.mov/llms.txt>)
  * [This page as Markdown](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/index.md>)

**On this page**

  1. Install
  2. Your first video
  3. What you just made

  5. Connect an agent

## Install

One binary, `ultrafast`, with `uf` as its short name. On macOS (Apple silicon) or Linux x86_64:

```
curl -fsSL https://ultrafast.mov/install.sh | sh
``` 

[The script](<https://ultrafast.mov/install.sh>) downloads the prebuilt release for your machine from [GitHub releases](<https://github.com/ultrafastmov/ultrafast/releases>), checks its SHA-256, unpacks it into `~/.ultrafast` and links `ultrafast` and `uf` into `~/.local/bin`. Or pick one of these:

```
brew install ultrafastmov/tap/ultrafast    # macOS and Linux, prebuilt
cargo install ultrafast                    # from crates.io, Rust 1.91 or later
docker run --gpus all ghcr.io/ultrafastmov/ultrafast:latest info
``` 

Or tell your agent “Go to ultrafast.mov and make…” and finish the sentence: it reads [llms.txt](<https://ultrafast.mov/llms.txt>), installs ultrafast and makes the video. Say “go to”: a bare “ultrafast.mov” reads to an agent like a video file.

It renders with **Metal** on macOS and **Vulkan** on Linux, and on Windows through WSL2 ([WINDOWS.md](<https://github.com/ultrafastmov/ultrafast/blob/main/docs/WINDOWS.md>)). Exports on Vulkan use ffmpeg, and on Linux voiceover and OCR use eSpeak NG and Tesseract. The Docker image includes all of them; the prebuilt binaries include everything else. No GPU? [ultrafast Cloud](<https://ultrafast.mov/cloud/>) is coming soon.

```
$ uf info
backend: vulkan
device:  NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090
``` 

## Your first video

Start from a template, look at it, then export it.

```
uf new vertical film.json                       # 1080×1920, 6 s, already looks finished
uf check film.json                              # problems, before anything renders
uf sheet film.json --count 9 --out sheet.png    # nine frames in one image
uf live film.json                               # plays it; edits show on the next frame
uf review film.json --safe social               # what a viewer would trip over
uf export film.json film.mp4                    # hardware-encoded mp4
``` 

Other templates: `title`, `square`, `promo`, `explainer` and `product`. Edit the words in `film.json` and run `uf export` again.

## What you just made

A video is one JSON document: a `format`, a graph of `nodes`, and the node to `output`. Nodes are sources (footage, type, shapes, 3D), effects and composites; any param can be animated.

```
{
  "version": 1,
  "format": { "width": 1920, "height": 1080, "fps": 60, "duration": 4.0 },
  "output": "comp",
  "nodes": {
    "bg":   { "op": "gradient", "params": { "a": "#0b0b1a", "b": "#2a1650" } },
    "disc": { "op": "shape", "params": {
      "kind": "circle", "color": "#ff7a2e", "size": [360, 360],
      "center": { "keys": [
        { "t": 0, "v": [560, 540], "ease": "in_out_cubic" },
        { "t": 4, "v": [1360, 540] }
      ] } } },
    "comp": { "op": "over", "inputs": { "fg": "disc", "bg": "bg" } }
  }
}
``` 

The whole vocabulary is in [the op reference](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/ops/>), and `uf ops` prints it as JSON. The shape of a document is in [The document](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/documents/>).

## The loop

This is how an agent works, and how you should too:

  1. **Start** from `uf new` or a copy of an example.
  2. **Check** : `uf check` reports unknown ops, misspelled params (with suggestions), wrongly shaped values, broken shaders and missing files, without rendering.
  3. **Look** : `uf sheet` for motion at a glance, `uf render --at 2.5` for one exact frame, `uf inspect --at 2.5` for which node drew what.
  4. **Review** : `uf review` renders the film and reports unreadable, clipped, overlapping, tiny or too-brief text, text under social app buttons, and flashing faster than three times a second.
  5. **Export** : `uf export`, hardware-encoded with sound and motion blur.

## Connect an agent

`uf mcp` serves all of this as 20 MCP tools over stdio. Frames and contact sheets come back as images, so the agent sees what it made.

```
claude mcp add ultrafast -- uf mcp
``` 

Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI and remote MCP over HTTP are on the [MCP page](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/mcp/>). Agents can also read [llms.txt](<https://ultrafast.mov/llms.txt>) and every page of these docs as Markdown.

## Run it as a service

`uf serve` puts the engine behind an HTTP API and remote MCP on your GPU, with one API key, for apps, the [SDKs](<https://ultrafast.mov/integrations/#sdks>) and agents on other machines.

```
uf serve --port 8080                   # prints its API key at first start
export ULTRAFAST_API_KEY=uf_live_...
jq '{document: ., output: {inline: true}}' film.json |
curl http://localhost:8080/v1/render -H "Authorization: Bearer $ULTRAFAST_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" --data-binary @- -o film.mp4
``` 

The requests are in [HTTP API](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/api/>). A hosted version, ultrafast Cloud, is coming soon: [join the waitlist](<https://ultrafast.mov/cloud/>).

## Next

  * [The document](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/documents/>): format, nodes, animation, timing and components.

  * [Examples](<https://ultrafast.mov/examples/>): every video there links to its document.

# The document format · ultrafast docs

> An ultrafast video is one JSON document: a format, a graph of nodes, animated params and timing windows. The full shape, with examples.

URL: https://ultrafast.mov/docs/documents/

Docs

# The document

A video is one JSON file. Here is its whole shape.

## Start

  * [Quickstart](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/>)
  * [The document](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/documents/>)

## Reference

  * [Ops](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/ops/>)
  * [CLI](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/cli/>)
  * [MCP server](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/mcp/>)
  * [HTTP API](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/api/>)

## For agents

  * [llms.txt](<https://ultrafast.mov/llms.txt>)
  * [This page as Markdown](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/documents/index.md>)

**On this page**

  1. Shape
  2. format
  3. nodes
  4. Params and animation
  5. timing
  6. components
  7. Assets, colour, type
  8. Schema and versions

## Shape

```
{
  "version": 1,
  "format": { "width": 1080, "height": 1920, "fps": 30, "duration": 10,
              "motion_blur": { "samples": 6, "shutter": 0.5 } },
  "nodes": {
    "<id>": { "op": "<op>", "params": { }, "inputs": { }, "timing": { } }
  },
  "components": { },
  "output": "<id of the node to render>"
}
``` 

Documents are plain files you can diff, template and edit. The engine reloads a document when it changes, so an agent can write it directly or through `uf edit`.

## format

  * `width`, `height`: any size, in pixels. Change them and frame-relative layout (blocks, captions, `fit`, stacks) follows.
  * `fps`, `duration`: frames per second and seconds.
  * `motion_blur`: `samples` and `shutter`, plus `max_samples` for whips and fast pans. Each moving layer is blurred on its own, as a compositor does; footage and shaders hold at the frame's time.

## nodes

Each node has an `op`, its `params`, its `inputs` (other nodes, by id, on named ports) and optional `timing`. Sources have no inputs; effects take a `source`; composites take `fg` and `bg`.

```
"clip":  { "op": "video", "params": { "src": "launch.mp4", "fit": "cover", "start": 12 } },
"grade": { "op": "grade", "inputs": { "source": "clip" }, "params": { "look": 2, "amount": 0.6 } },
"title": { "op": "block", "params": { "kind": "title", "title": "Artemis I", "kicker": "16 Nov 2022" } },
"comp":  { "op": "over", "inputs": { "fg": "title", "bg": "grade" } }
``` 

Generators (`solid`, `gradient`, `noise`, shaders) are infinite: crop or transform them into panels. Paths and text stay vector until they are rasterized, so a `transform` directly on them stays sharp at any scale. The planner fuses chains of nodes into one GPU kernel and skips what can't be seen.

## Params and animation

Any param can be a constant or animated:

```
"size": 64
"position": { "keys": [ { "t": 0, "v": [540, 2100], "ease": "out_expo" },
                        { "t": 0.8, "v": [540, 960] } ] }
"rotation": { "keys": [ { "t": 0, "v": 0 }, { "t": 1, "v": 10 } ], "repeat": "pingpong" }
"position": { "wiggle": { "frequency": 2, "amplitude": 10, "base": [540, 960] } }
"opacity":  { "expr": "0.5 + 0.5 * sin(t * 3)" }
``` 

  * **Keys** : `t` in seconds, `v` the value, `ease` a name (`in_out_cubic`, `out_expo`, `out_back`, `spring`...) or a CSS-style bezier `{"bezier": [0.16, 1, 0.3, 1]}`. `repeat`: `cycle` or `pingpong`.
  * **Drivers** : `wiggle`, `oscillate`, and `audio`, which follows a soundtrack band so a param pulses with the music.
  * **Expressions** : `{"expr": "..."}`, a formula of `t`, with a list for vectors.

## timing

```
"timing": { "in": 2, "out": 6, "offset": 2, "speed": 0.5 }
``` 

  * `in`, `out`: when the node is on screen. Outside its window a composite passes its background through and an effect passes its source; neither costs anything.
  * `offset`: where the node's local time zero sits in its parent's time. `speed`: local seconds per parent second (negative plays backwards). `loop`: local time wraps at this duration.
  * Windows compose through nesting. For cuts between shots, prefer `transition` nodes (crossfade, dip, wipe, push, slide, iris, zoom, dissolve, glitch, blur); each shot renders only while it is on screen.

## components

A component is a small document with its own params and inputs, used like an op. `"$name"` inside a component refers to one of its params. Components are flattened before planning, so they cost nothing at render time. `uf import-svg` and `uf import-lottie` write SVG artwork and Lottie animations as components with every part editable.

## Assets, colour, type

  * File paths (footage, images, fonts, SVG, Lottie, audio) are relative to the document.
  * Colours are sRGB hex (`#ff48b0`, `#ff48b080`) or 0–1 arrays with straight alpha. Compositing is in linear light; set `"space": "srgb"` on an `over`, `blend` or `gradient` to blend the way CSS and Figma do.
  * Fonts: a family name (any Google Font is fetched once by name), a font file, or a bundled face (`ultrafast:display`, `ultrafast:sans`, `ultrafast:serif`, `ultrafast:mono`, `ultrafast:wide`). Variable fonts animate any axis with `axis_<tag>`.

## Schema and versions

Documents carry `"version": 1`. The JSON Schema is published at [ultrafast.mov/schema/v1.json](<https://ultrafast.mov/schema/v1.json>) for editor completion and validation; `uf schema` prints the same file, and `uf ops` the vocabulary with every param's type and default. Changes within a version are additive.


---

# MCP server · 20 tools · ultrafast docs

> ultrafast as MCP tools for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI and any MCP client: local over stdio with uf mcp, or remote over Streamable HTTP from your own uf serve with an API key.

URL: https://ultrafast.mov/docs/mcp/

Docs

# MCP server

20 tools that let an agent write a video, look at it, fix it and export it, without a shell.

## Start

  * [Quickstart](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/>)
  * [The document](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/documents/>)

## Reference

  * [Ops](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/ops/>)
  * [CLI](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/cli/>)
  * [MCP server](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/mcp/>)
  * [HTTP API](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/api/>)

## For agents

  * [llms.txt](<https://ultrafast.mov/llms.txt>)
  * [This page as Markdown](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/mcp/index.md>)

**On this page**

  1. Local, over stdio
  2. Remote, over HTTP
  3. The tools
  4. How agents use them

## Local, over stdio

`uf mcp` is a stdio MCP server (JSON-RPC 2.0, one message per line). Renders run on your GPU.

```
claude mcp add ultrafast -- uf mcp
``` 

```
[mcp_servers.ultrafast]
command = "uf"
args = ["mcp"]
``` 

```
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "ultrafast": { "command": "uf", "args": ["mcp"] }
  }
}
``` 

Documents stay plain JSON files. The server keeps a renderer per document, so repeated frames are fast, and reloads a file when it changes, whether the agent edits it with `ultrafast_edit` or writes it directly.

## Remote, over HTTP

`ultrafast serve` answers MCP over Streamable HTTP at `/mcp`, with its API key as a bearer token, for agent frameworks and any client that can't run a local process. It serves the 16 tools that need no local files; they take the document and asset ids instead of file paths; frames and sheets come back as images and exports as download links.

```
claude mcp add --transport http ultrafast http://localhost:8080/mcp \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $ULTRAFAST_API_KEY"
``` 

A hosted server with OAuth sign-in, for the ChatGPT app and the Claude connector, comes with [ultrafast Cloud](<https://ultrafast.mov/cloud/>).

## The tools

tool| does  
---|---  
`ultrafast_ops`| The op vocabulary: ports, params, types, defaults, docs.  
`ultrafast_new`| Write a template (`vertical`, `title`, `square`, `promo`, `explainer`, `product`) to a path.  
`ultrafast_check`| Problems in a document, static and render-time.  
`ultrafast_frame`| One exact frame, returned as an image.  
`ultrafast_sheet`| A labelled contact sheet of frames, returned as an image.  
`ultrafast_review`| Renders the film and reports unreadable, too-brief, clipped, overlapping or tiny text, unsafe areas and seizure-risk flashing.  
`ultrafast_inspect`| What is on screen at a time: each element's node, bounds and words.  
`ultrafast_edit`| Apply an edit batch to the document file, atomically.  
`ultrafast_export`| Encode to MP4, MOV (ProRes), WebM, a GIF, a PNG or EXR sequence or sound alone, at any size, frame rate and quality level, transparent where the codec allows.  
`ultrafast_estimate`| Rendered minutes, GPU seconds and the time to the first byte, before rendering.  
`ultrafast_batch`| One document, a video per row of a CSV or JSON file.  
`ultrafast_profile`| GPU milliseconds per render group, for slow films.  
`ultrafast_beats`| Tempo, beats, downbeats and onsets of a soundtrack.  
`ultrafast_voiceover`| Speak a script to WAV with every word's time, for audio and captions.  
`ultrafast_import_svg`| An SVG as an editable component, or added to a document.  
`ultrafast_decompose`| A finished video as an editable document: plate, vector layers with their motion, gradients, type read back as text in its matched font.  
`ultrafast_match_font`| A text node's font, size, baseline, tracking and colour, from a video frame.  
`ultrafast_ocr`| The text in a video frame, with word boxes and a draft of text nodes.  
`ultrafast_measure`| Glyph metrics of a line of text.  
`ultrafast_outline`| A line of text as SVG path data.  
  
## How agents use them

  1. `ultrafast_new` or write the JSON; `ultrafast_ops` when unsure of a param.
  2. `ultrafast_check` until it's clean.
  3. `ultrafast_sheet` to see the motion; `ultrafast_inspect` to find the node behind a pixel.
  4. `ultrafast_review`; fix what it reports with `ultrafast_edit`.
  5. `ultrafast_export`.

The [MCP server overview](<https://ultrafast.mov/mcp/>) shows this loop on a real film, with the clients tested and how it differs from other video MCP servers.

The ultrafast skill teaches agents the document and this loop: `npx skills add ultrafastmov/ultrafast`. In Claude Code, the plugin brings the skill and `uf mcp` together: `claude plugin marketplace add ultrafastmov/ultrafast`, then `claude plugin install ultrafast@ultrafast`.

Agents that read docs can start from [llms.txt](<https://ultrafast.mov/llms.txt>); every page here is also available as Markdown at `index.md`.


---

# CLI reference · ultrafast docs

> Every ultrafast command: new, check, sheet, render, review, inspect, live, export, serve, mcp and more. The CLI is ultrafast, or uf for short.

URL: https://ultrafast.mov/docs/cli/

Docs  
  
# The CLI

`ultrafast`, or `uf` for short. Every command answers in JSON or in files you can look at.

## Start

  * [Quickstart](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/>)
  * [The document](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/documents/>)

## Reference

  * [Ops](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/ops/>)
  * [CLI](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/cli/>)
  * [MCP server](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/mcp/>)
  * [HTTP API](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/api/>)

## For agents

  * [llms.txt](<https://ultrafast.mov/llms.txt>)
  * [This page as Markdown](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/cli/index.md>)

**On this page**

  1. Make
  2. Export
  3. Look and review
  4. Learn the vocabulary
  5. Import and rebuild
  6. Sound
  7. Speed
  8. Serve
  9. Cloud

## Make

`uf new <template> <out.json>`| Start from a template: `vertical`, `title`, `square`, `promo`, `explainer`, `product`.  
---|---  
`uf check <doc.json>`| Problems without rendering: unknown ops, misspelled params, bad values, broken shaders, missing files.  
`uf edit <doc.json> <edits.json>`| Apply an edit batch; prints what kind of change it was.  
`uf live <doc.json> [--port 7878]`| A realtime player and JSON-lines edit server; reloads the file when it changes. `--compare ref.mp4` shows a reference split against it.  
`uf send '<json>'`| Send one request to a live session.  
`uf record <doc> <script> <out.mp4>`| Play a document while applying a script of edits, and film the player.  
`uf export <doc> <out>`| Encode the film; the format follows `<out>`. H.264 and HEVC encode on the GPU with zero readback. All the options are under Export.  
`uf batch <doc> --data rows.csv`| One document, a video per row of a CSV, JSON or JSON-lines file. A column named `node.param` sets that param; other columns name the files: `--out 'out/{name}.mp4'`. `--docs DIR` writes each row's document instead.  
  
## Export

One document gives every deliverable. The same settings work as `uf export` flags, [MCP](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/mcp/>) tool arguments and the [API](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/api/>)'s `output`. Settings that don't go together are refused before anything renders.

Formats| `.mp4`, `.mov`, `.mkv`, `.webm`, `.gif`; a folder (`frames/`) or a pattern (`frames/{frame:05}.exr`) for a PNG or EXR sequence, with the sound beside it as `audio.wav`; `.wav`, `.mp3`, `.m4a`, `.flac`, `.opus` for the sound alone. `--format` names one.  
---|---  
`--quality draft|standard|high|master`| `draft` is a fast preview: no motion blur and the fastest encode. `standard` is the default. `high` takes more motion-blur samples and a slower encode, for uploads that get re-encoded. `master` takes twice the samples and the best encode. The shutter never changes, so the look stays the document's.  
`--size 720p|1080p|1440p|4k|WxH`, `--scale S`| Renders at that size, sharp; it is not an upscale. `720p` is the short side, so a vertical film stays vertical.  
`--fps N`| Another frame rate (`29.97` and `30000/1001` work); the film plays at the same speed. GIFs default to at most 30.  
`--codec h264|hevc|av1|vp9|prores`| The default is H.264 (VP9 in `.webm`). `--prores-profile proxy|light|standard|hq|4444|4444-xq` defaults to `hq`.  
`--alpha`| Keeps transparency: ProRes 4444 in `.mov`, VP9 in `.webm`, GIF, PNG and EXR. Leave the full-frame background out of the document.  
`--crf N`, `--bitrate 8M`| Constant quality on the codec's scale, or an average bitrate, instead of the quality level's.  
`--audio-codec aac|opus|mp3|flac|pcm|pcm-24`, `--audio-bitrate 192k`, `--no-audio`| The sound in the file: AAC by default, Opus in WebM, PCM with ProRes.  
`--loops N`| GIF: how many more times it plays after the first. `0` plays once; the default is forever.  
`--from S`, `--to S`, `--workers N`| A range of the film; several renderers on the GPU at once.  
  
```
uf export film.json film.mp4 --quality draft --size 720p     # watch the motion
uf export film.json film.mp4 --size 4k --quality high         # a sharp 4K upload
uf export film.json overlay.mov --codec prores --alpha        # ProRes 4444 for an editor
uf export film.json web.webm --alpha                          # VP9 with alpha for a page
uf export film.json teaser.gif --size 480p --fps 15           # a GIF
uf export film.json plates/ --alpha                           # PNG frames and audio.wav
``` 

## Look and review

`uf sheet <doc> [--count N]`| A labelled contact sheet of frames: motion at a glance.  
---|---  
`uf render <doc> --at 2.5 --out f.png`| One exact frame; `--size 4k` or `--scale 2` renders it larger.  
`uf frames <doc> --out-dir DIR`| Every frame (or every Nth) as PNG.  
`uf inspect <doc> --at T [--point X,Y]`| What is on screen at a time: each element's node, bounds and words; with `--point`, the topmost element there.  
`uf review <doc> [--safe margin|social]`| Render the film and report what viewers would trip over: unreadable, too-brief, clipped, overlapping or tiny text; text under social app buttons; flashing faster than 3 per second.  
  
## Learn the vocabulary

`uf ops`| Every op, its ports, params, types and defaults, as JSON. The same as the [op reference](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/ops/>).  
---|---  
`uf schema`| The document format as JSON Schema, the same as [/schema/v1.json](<https://ultrafast.mov/schema/v1.json>).  
`uf measure '<text params>'`| Glyph-by-glyph metrics of a line of text, for hand layout.  
`uf outline '<text params>'`| A line of text as SVG path data, for morphs and vector work.  
`uf info`| The GPU and backend in use.  
  
## Import and rebuild

`uf import-svg <file.svg>`| An SVG as an editable component: one path per shape, gradients, strokes, text as outlines.  
---|---  
`uf import-lottie <anim.json>`| A Lottie animation as editable paths and keyframes.  
`uf decompose <video> --out-dir DIR`| Split a motion-graphics video into a still plate and vector layers keyed frame by frame.  
`uf reconstruct <video> --out-dir DIR`| A whole video as an editable draft: shots, text layers with matched fonts, backgrounds, fades.  
`uf probe`, `extract`, `compare`, `fit`, `fit-motion`, `match-font`, `plate`, `ocr`, `matte`| Refine a reconstruction: shots, reference frames, PSNR and SSIM, fitted params and motion, fonts, plates, text, mattes. Text is read with Apple Vision on macOS and Tesseract elsewhere; `matte` needs macOS.  
`uf faces <video>`| Face tracks, who is talking and the cuts: what a `clip_camera` follows. A `clip_camera` without `faces` tracks them itself.  
  
## Sound

`uf beats <audio or video>`| Tempo, beat grid, downbeats and onsets as JSON: cut on the beat.  
---|---  
`uf voiceover '<text>' out.wav words.json`| Speak a script and write the time of every word, for `audio` and `captions` nodes. The system voices on macOS, eSpeak NG elsewhere.  
  
## Speed

`uf estimate <doc>`| What an export costs before it runs: rendered minutes, GPU seconds timed on sampled frames, and the time to the first byte. Give it the export flags (`--size 4k --quality high`) to estimate that export. `--json` for the numbers.  
---|---  
`uf bench <doc>`| GPU throughput with no readback.  
`uf profile <doc> [--from T]`| GPU time per render group: which nodes cost what, and how many motion-blur samples each runs.  
`uf plan <doc>`| How the graph fused into kernels.  
`uf warm <doc>...`| Compile and cache every kernel the documents need, so a fresh instance starts compiled.  
  
## Serve

`uf mcp`| 20 MCP tools over stdio. See [MCP server](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/mcp/>).  
---|---  
`uf serve [--port 8080]`| The render service on your GPU: the [HTTP API](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/api/>) (renders, uploads, frames, sheets, check, review, estimate) and remote MCP at `/mcp`, with one API key and files on local disk. `uf serve key` prints a new key.  
`uf batch`| With no document: export `<doc.json> <out.mp4>` per line of stdin with one warm renderer.  
  
## Cloud

ultrafast Cloud, which will run these commands on hosted GPUs, is coming soon: [join the waitlist](<https://ultrafast.mov/cloud/>). Until then every command runs on your own GPU, and `uf serve` shares it over HTTP.


---

# HTTP API · ultrafast docs

> Render ultrafast documents over HTTP with uf serve on your own GPU: renders, frames, sheets, check, review, estimates and uploads, with one API key.

URL: https://ultrafast.mov/docs/api/

Docs

# HTTP API

Render documents over HTTP from `uf serve` on your own GPU, with one API key and files on local disk.

## Start

  * [Quickstart](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/>)
  * [The document](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/documents/>)

## Reference

  * [Ops](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/ops/>)
  * [CLI](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/cli/>)
  * [MCP server](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/mcp/>)
  * [HTTP API](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/api/>)

## For agents

  * [llms.txt](<https://ultrafast.mov/llms.txt>)
  * [This page as Markdown](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/api/index.md>)

**On this page**

  1. Authentication
  2. POST /v1/render
  3. Jobs and webhooks
  4. POST /v1/estimate
  5. POST /v1/frame
  6. Check and review
  7. Uploads
  8. Errors and limits
  9. Cloud-only parts

## Authentication

Start the server with `uf serve` (or the [Docker image](<https://ultrafast.mov/integrations/#self-host>)); the base URL is `http://localhost:8080` unless you pass `--port` or `--host`. Send its API key as a bearer token: with none set, it makes one at first start and prints it, and `uf serve key` prints a new one. The SDKs read `ULTRAFAST_BASE_URL` and `ULTRAFAST_API_KEY`.

```
Authorization: Bearer uf_live_...
Content-Type: application/json
``` 

## POST /v1/render

A document in, a video out: MP4, MOV, WebM, a GIF, a PNG or EXR sequence, or sound alone, at any size and frame rate. Short renders can come back in the response; anything longer goes to storage and returns a receipt.

```
{
  "document": { "version": 1, "format": { }, "nodes": { }, "output": "comp" },
  "output": {
    "inline": true,
    "quality": "draft",
    "size": "720p",
    "audio": true,
    "range": null
  }
}
``` 

  * `output.inline: true`: the file is the response body (up to 32 MiB), with its own content type. Otherwise it is stored and you get a receipt with a signed URL.
  * `output.format`: `mp4` (default), `mov`, `mkv`, `webm`, `gif`; `png` or `exr` for an image sequence, delivered as a zip with the sound as `audio.wav`; `wav`, `mp3`, `m4a`, `flac` or `opus` for the sound alone. `output.name`'s extension picks it too.
  * `output.codec`: `h264` (default), `hevc`, `av1`, `vp9` or `prores` (`prores_profile`: `proxy` to `4444-xq`, default `hq`). `output.alpha: true` keeps transparency in ProRes 4444, VP9, GIF, PNG and EXR.
  * `output.quality`: `draft` (a fast preview without motion blur), `standard` (default), `high` or `master`. `crf` or `bitrate` (`"8M"`) override its encoder setting.
  * `output.size`: `720p`, `1080p`, `1440p`, `4k` or `"WxH"`, rendered at that size, sharp, not scaled up; or `scale`. `output.fps`: another frame rate; the film plays at the same speed. Minutes count the size you render.
  * `audio`, `audio_codec`, `audio_bitrate`; `loops` for GIFs; `output.range`: `[from, to]` seconds. Settings that don't go together are a `400` before anything renders.
  * `output.uri` (Cloud only): write to your own bucket (`s3://`, `gs://`, `r2://`) instead, create-only, so a retry never overwrites a finished video.

```
{
  "status": "rendered",
  "url": "http://localhost:8080/v1/files/renders/render_01M7.../film.mp4?expires=...&sig=...",
  "duration": 11.6,
  "frames": 348,
  "bytes": 6620112,
  "sha256": "2b7e...",
  "video": { "width": 1080, "height": 1920, "fps": 30, "format": "mp4", "codec": "h264", "quality": "standard" },
  "minutes": 0.19,
  "timings": { "plan_s": 0.03, "render_s": 1.71, "encode_s": 0.22, "total_s": 2.2 }
}
``` 

## Jobs and webhooks

Planned for [ultrafast Cloud](<https://ultrafast.mov/cloud/>), and not in `uf serve`: long or batch renders as jobs, with a webhook called when each is done. A self-hosted server answers `/v1/jobs` with `501` and the code `cloud_only`.

Webhooks are signed with your webhook secret (`GET /v1/me`; `Ultrafast-Signature: sha256=` and the hex HMAC-SHA256 of the body) and retried with backoff for 24 hours.

## POST /v1/estimate

What a document will cost before it renders: rendered minutes, GPU seconds and the time to the first byte, from the same plan the renderer runs. A few sampled frames render on the GPU and nothing is encoded. Send the render request's `output` along (`{"size": "4k", "quality": "high"}`) to estimate that render.

```
{ "minutes": 0.2, "gpu_seconds": 2.1, "first_byte_s": 3.0, "usd": null }
``` 

`usd` stays null unless whoever runs the server sets a price per minute.

## POST /v1/frame

One frame as PNG or JPEG: `{"document": {...}, "at": 2.5, "format": "png"}`. `POST /v1/sheet` returns a labelled contact sheet the same way.

## Check and review

`POST /v1/check` with `{"document": {...}}` returns `{"ok", "issues"}`, the same as `uf check`. `POST /v1/review` renders the film and returns what `uf review` finds: `{"document": {...}, "safe": "social"}`.

## Uploads

Footage, images, fonts and audio go up once and are referenced by id in documents.

```
curl http://localhost:8080/v1/uploads -H "Authorization: Bearer $ULTRAFAST_API_KEY" \
  -F file=@interview.mp4
# {"id": "asset_7Kq...", "uri": "asset://7Kq...", "bytes": 48211002, ...}
``` 

Then use `"src": "asset://7Kq..."` in a `video`, `image`, `audio` or `captions` node. Public `https://` URLs work too. Documents sent to the server never read local paths; the SDKs upload a document's local files for you.

## Errors and limits

Errors come back as `{"error": {"status", "code", "message", "retry"}}`.

status| meaning  
---|---  
`400`| The document doesn't pass `check`. The body lists the issues, the same as `uf check`.  
`401`| Missing or wrong API key.  
`403`| The document reads a local path, or a host the server doesn't allow.  
`413`| Inline output over 32 MiB: leave out `inline` to store it and get a receipt.  
`422`| An input couldn't be fetched.  
`429`| The queue is full: the server renders one request at a time, and 16 more can wait.  
`501`| `cloud_only`: jobs, `output.uri` and bucket inputs are planned for ultrafast Cloud.  
  
A render stops after 10 minutes of work. The limits on output length, input size and the queue are settings; see [SELF_HOST.md](<https://github.com/ultrafastmov/ultrafast/blob/main/docs/service/SELF_HOST.md>).

## Cloud-only parts

A few parts of the API wait for [ultrafast Cloud](<https://ultrafast.mov/cloud/>): jobs with signed webhooks, writing renders to your own S3, R2 or GCS bucket with `output.uri`, reading inputs from buckets, and many keys with sign-in. `uf serve` answers them with `501` and the code `cloud_only`, and the SDKs raise `CloudOnly` (Python) or `CloudOnlyError` (TypeScript). It has no billing, so `/v1/estimate` gives a price only if you set `ULTRAFAST_USD_PER_MINUTE`. The full list of settings is in [SELF_HOST.md](<https://github.com/ultrafastmov/ultrafast/blob/main/docs/service/SELF_HOST.md>).


---

# Use cases · Make videos by asking · ultrafast

> Social posts, podcast clips, documentaries, explainers, data stories, launch films and title sequences, made by asking an agent: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or Gemini CLI with ultrafast.

URL: https://ultrafast.mov/use-cases/

Use cases

# Ask your agent for a video.

Describe it to Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or Gemini CLI with ultrafast connected. The agent writes the document, ultrafast checks every frame, and the agent exports the file. No timeline, no editor.

[Connect your agent](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/#agents>) [See examples](<https://ultrafast.mov/examples/>)

How it goes

## Three steps.

  1. ### Ask

Say what it's for, how long, and what's in it. Give the agent footage, photos or a logo if you have them.

  2. ### Look

The agent reads contact sheets and fixes what `review` finds; `uf live` plays the draft for you. Say what to change: words, colours, music, length.

  3. ### Export

An MP4 in each size you need, 9:16 to 21:9. The document stays in your folder, so next week's changes start from it.

Twelve things agents made

## Made by asking.

Each card gives the brief in a sentence. Every film here is a real render, made by a coding agent with ultrafast; its document is on the [examples page](<https://ultrafast.mov/examples/>).

[Video: Pottery class teaser](https://ultrafast.mov/media/examples/clay.mp4)

### Title sequences

For builders

## Put it inside your product.

Your users ask your app for a video; your agent writes the document; ultrafast renders it on your GPU with `uf serve`. They never see a timeline.

[Read the quickstart](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/>)[Integrations](<https://ultrafast.mov/integrations/>)

```
from ultrafastmov import Ultrafast

uf = Ultrafast(base_url="http://localhost:8080")  # your uf serve

doc = uf.load("teaser.json")     # what your agent wrote
issues = uf.check(doc)           # before a frame renders
video = uf.render(doc)
video.save("teaser.mp4")
``` 

Questions

## Common questions.

Do I need to know how to edit video?

No. Describe what you want to your agent in plain words, the way you'd brief a person. The agent writes the document, ultrafast checks every frame for unreadable or clipped text, and the agent exports the file.

Which agents can do this?

Any agent that can run an MCP server or a shell: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Gemini CLI connect to `uf mcp` in one line. See [MCP](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/mcp/>). The ChatGPT app and the Claude connector come with [ultrafast Cloud](<https://ultrafast.mov/cloud/>).

Can I use my own footage, photos and logo?

Yes. Give your agent the files. ultrafast works with video, photos, SVG logos, Lottie animations, music and voiceover, and any Google Font by name.

How long does a video take?

The render takes seconds: each film on this page exported in under 8 seconds on one RTX 5090. Writing and reviewing the document takes your agent longer, depending on the model and the film.

Can I change it afterwards?

Yes. The video is a JSON document file, so ask for changes any time: new words, another size, a different song. The agent edits the nodes that change and leaves the rest as it was.

## Make the first one.

Free and open source. Install it, connect your agent, and ask.

`curl -fsSL https://ultrafast.mov/install.sh | sh` [Read the quickstart](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/>)

Want it hosted? [Join the ultrafast Cloud waitlist](<https://ultrafast.mov/cloud/>).

Coding agents

## Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI.

Run `uf mcp` on your machine and the agent gets 20 tools: it writes the document, looks at frames and contact sheets, fixes what `review` finds and exports. The [MCP server page](<https://ultrafast.mov/mcp/>) shows that loop on a real film.

### Claude Code

```
claude mcp add ultrafast -- uf mcp
``` 

### Codex

```
[mcp_servers.ultrafast]
command = "uf"
args = ["mcp"]
``` 

### Cursor

```
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "ultrafast": { "command": "uf", "args": ["mcp"] }
  }
}
``` 

### Gemini CLI

```
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "ultrafast": { "command": "uf", "args": ["mcp"] }
  }
}
``` 

Each agent also gets the ultrafast skill: `npx skills add ultrafastmov/ultrafast`. In Claude Code, the plugin brings both: `claude plugin marketplace add ultrafastmov/ultrafast`, then `claude plugin install ultrafast@ultrafast`.

Remote MCP

## From your own server.

`uf serve` answers MCP over Streamable HTTP at `/mcp`, with its API key as a bearer token. The tools take documents and asset ids instead of file paths; frames and contact sheets come back as images, so the agent sees its work.

A hosted server with OAuth sign-in comes with [ultrafast Cloud](<https://ultrafast.mov/cloud/>).

[MCP docs](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/mcp/#remote>)

```
claude mcp add --transport http ultrafast \
  http://localhost:8080/mcp \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $ULTRAFAST_API_KEY"
``` 

```
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "ultrafast": {
      "url": "http://localhost:8080/mcp",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer uf_live_..." }
    }
  }
}
``` 

SDKs

## Python and TypeScript.

`render`, `frame`, `sheet`, `check`, `review`, `estimate` and `upload`, against your own `uf serve`. Local footage, images and fonts in the document are uploaded for you.

```
from ultrafastmov import Ultrafast

# your uf serve, and the key it printed
uf = Ultrafast(base_url="http://localhost:8080")

doc = uf.load("film.json")
for issue in uf.review(doc):
    print(issue.kind, issue.node, issue.message)
uf.render(doc).save("film.mp4")
``` 

```
import { Ultrafast } from "ultrafastmov";

// your uf serve, and the key it printed
const uf = new Ultrafast({ baseUrl: "http://localhost:8080" });

const doc = await uf.load("film.json");
await (await uf.sheet(doc, { count: 9 })).save("sheet.png");
const render = await uf.render(doc);
await render.save("film.mp4");
``` 

Agent frameworks

## Starters for the frameworks you build on.

Starter apps for the Vercel AI SDK, the OpenAI Agents SDK, LangGraph and Mastra: an agent that takes a brief, works through the `/mcp` tools of your `uf serve` and returns a reviewed MP4. They're in the `starters/` folder of the repo.

[Starters on GitHub](<https://github.com/ultrafastmov/ultrafast/tree/main/starters>)

```
from agents import Agent, Runner
from agents.mcp import MCPServerStreamableHttp

async with MCPServerStreamableHttp(params={
    "url": "http://localhost:8080/mcp",
    "headers": {"Authorization": f"Bearer {key}"},
}) as ultrafast:
    agent = Agent(
        name="Editor",
        mcp_servers=[ultrafast],
        instructions="Make it, review it, export it.",
    )
    result = await Runner.run(agent, "A 15 s launch promo")
``` 

HTTP API

## One request, one video.

POST a document to your `uf serve`, get an MP4 back.

[HTTP API docs](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/api/>)

```
jq '{document: ., output: {inline: true}}' film.json |
curl http://localhost:8080/v1/render \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ULTRAFAST_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data-binary @- -o film.mp4
``` 

Self-host

## Your GPU.

The render service is open source: the HTTP API and remote MCP on one machine with a GPU, one API key, files on local disk. Enough to build against and to share one box on a small team.

Jobs with signed webhooks, output to your own bucket, sign-in and GPUs that scale are planned for [ultrafast Cloud](<https://ultrafast.mov/cloud/>).

[SELF_HOST.md](<https://github.com/ultrafastmov/ultrafast/blob/main/docs/service/SELF_HOST.md>)

```
docker run --gpus all -p 8080:8080 -v ultrafast:/data \
  ghcr.io/ultrafastmov/ultrafast:latest serve
``` 

CLI and live player

## And a shell.

`uf live film.json` plays a document while you or an agent edit it; parameter edits show on the next frame.

[CLI reference](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/cli/>)

```
uf new vertical film.json
uf check film.json
uf live film.json
uf review film.json --safe social
uf export film.json film.mp4
```

# Video MCP server for agents · Shot on the GPU · ultrafast

> A video MCP server for Claude Code, Cursor and any MCP client: 20 tools to write, look at, review and export video, rendered on your GPU. Open source.

URL: https://ultrafast.mov/mcp/

# Shot on the GPU.

Shaders, 3D, motion type and camera optics, written by your agent and rendered on the GPU. Open source.

The ultrafast MCP server gives your agent 20 tools to write a video, look at its frames, review them and export the file, on your own GPU.

`curl -fsSL https://ultrafast.mov/install.sh | sh` Set up your client

macOS on Apple silicon and Linux x86_64. Every parameter is in the [MCP reference](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/mcp/>).

ultrafast MCP server, v0.1.1

tools over stdio, uf mcp
    20
tools over HTTP, /mcp
    16
frames and sheets
    images
review reads
    every frame
licence
    Apache-2.0 or MIT

In the official MCP Registry as io.github.ultrafastmov/ultrafast

## What your agent sees.

Frames and contact sheets come back as images. The review comes back as findings, each naming a node, a time and a fix.

  1. ### It looks

`ultrafast_frame` returns one exact frame and `ultrafast_sheet` a labelled contact sheet, as images in the conversation. `ultrafast_inspect` names the node behind anything on screen.

  2. ### It reviews

`ultrafast_review` renders every frame. It reports text that is unreadable, clipped, overlapping, too small or too brief, text under social-app buttons, and flashing that risks seizures.

  3. ### It fixes and exports

`ultrafast_edit` changes the nodes a finding names and leaves the rest. `ultrafast_export` writes MP4, MOV, WebM, a GIF or an image sequence, at any size.

![Contact sheet of the first draft, frames at 0.55, 2.6, 4.5 and 7.5 seconds. Frame one is a white flash, the title runs off the right edge, the studio name is too dark to read and the details are tiny.](https://ultrafast.mov/img/proof_draft.webp)

  1. **flashing** more than 3 flashes per second: a photosensitive seizure risk (WCAG 2.3.1)
  2. **clipped** "Pottery class" runs off the frame (right by 40 px)
  3. **low contrast ×2** "HALDEN CLAY STUDIO" never reaches readable contrast (best 1.6:1, want 3:1 or more); "118 TANNER STREET" 1.6:1
  4. **too brief** "First class free" is readable for 0.4 s; 3 words need about 0.9 s
  5. **small text ×3** set at 20 px; below about 24 px it is hard to read on a phone

![Contact sheet of the second draft at the same moments: no flash, the title fits, the studio name and the details read.](https://ultrafast.mov/img/proof_approved.webp) 0 findings

  1. `sheet`: the draft, as an image
  2. `review`: 8 findings, each with a fix
  3. `edit`: the nodes they name
  4. `export`: after 0 findings, in 1.68 s

The pottery teaser from the [examples](<https://ultrafast.mov/examples/>): its first draft and its second, at the same four moments. The review read all 300 frames in 4.7 s. These sheets and reviews came from the CLI (`uf sheet`, `uf review --safe social`), which runs the same code as the tools. The second version's document is [clay-v1.json](<https://ultrafast.mov/examples/clay-v1.json>).

## 20 tools, in six groups.

As `uf mcp` lists them in v0.1.1. The remote server has the 16 that don't read or write files on your machine.

### Write

  * `ultrafast_ops`: the op vocabulary, with every port, param, type and default.
  * `ultrafast_new`: a template to start from: vertical, title, square, promo, explainer or product.
  * `ultrafast_edit`: an edit batch applied to the document, atomically.

### Look

  * `ultrafast_frame`: one exact frame, as an image.
  * `ultrafast_sheet`: a labelled contact sheet of frames, as one image.
  * `ultrafast_inspect`: what is on screen at a time, with each element's node, bounds and words.

### Check and review

  * `ultrafast_check`: problems before rendering: unknown ops, misspelled params, broken shaders, missing files or fonts.
  * `ultrafast_review`: renders the film and reports what a viewer would trip over, with the node and a fix.

### Render and export

  * `ultrafast_export`: MP4, MOV, MKV or WebM, a GIF, PNG or EXR frames, or sound alone, at any size and frame rate.
  * `ultrafast_estimate`: rendered minutes, GPU seconds and the time to the first frame, before rendering.
  * `ultrafast_batch`: one document, a video per row of data.
  * `ultrafast_profile`: GPU milliseconds per render group, for slow films.

### Import

  * `ultrafast_import_svg`: an SVG as an editable component.
  * `ultrafast_decompose`: a finished motion-graphics video as an editable document. Local only.
  * `ultrafast_ocr`: the text in a video frame, with word boxes and draft text nodes. Local only.
  * `ultrafast_match_font`: a text node's font, size, tracking and colour, from a video frame. Local only.

### Sound and type

  * `ultrafast_beats`: tempo, beats, downbeats and onsets of a soundtrack.
  * `ultrafast_voiceover`: a script spoken to WAV, with every word's time. Local only.
  * `ultrafast_measure`: glyph metrics of a line of text.
  * `ultrafast_outline`: a line of text as SVG path data.

The server also tells the agent the loop when it connects: ops, a template, check until clean, look at sheets and frames, review and fix, then export. “Always look at a sheet before exporting.” Parameters for every tool are in the [MCP reference](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/mcp/#tools>).

``` 

Tested with Claude Code 2.1.325: a model run used new, check, sheet (and saw the image), inspect, edit and export.

### Remote, from your own uf serve

```

``` 

16 tools over Streamable HTTP, with the server's API key as a bearer token. Documents travel inline; exports come back as download links. Tested with Claude Code over HTTP, and with MCP Inspector, which called all 16 tools.

### The MCP Registry and the MCP bundles

```
io.github.ultrafastmov/ultrafast

ultrafast-0.1.1-macos-arm64.mcpb
ultrafast-0.1.1-linux-x86_64.mcpb
``` 

The name in the [official MCP Registry](<https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0/servers?search=io.github.ultrafastmov/ultrafast>), which points to the two bundles on the [v0.1.1 release](<https://github.com/ultrafastmov/ultrafast/releases/tag/v0.1.1>): a .mcpb bundle for Claude Desktop on a [Mac with Apple silicon](<https://github.com/ultrafastmov/ultrafast/releases/download/v0.1.1/ultrafast-0.1.1-macos-arm64.mcpb>), and one for [Linux x86_64](<https://github.com/ultrafastmov/ultrafast/releases/download/v0.1.1/ultrafast-0.1.1-linux-x86_64.mcpb>). Each carries the binary and asks for one setting: the folder for documents and videos, `~/ultrafast` by default.

Codex and the JSON config for Claude Desktop are in the [MCP reference](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/mcp/#local>); neither has been tested yet. Any other MCP client that runs a stdio server, or connects over Streamable HTTP with a header, takes the same settings.

## How it differs from other video MCP servers.

Most video MCP servers wrap FFmpeg to edit files you already have, or call a hosted API. ultrafast makes the frames.

### FFmpeg wrappers

  * They cut, trim, join and convert video files you already have.
  * FFmpeg does the work. The tools pass it the commands.

### Hosted APIs

  * The tools send the job to a rendering service and get a result back.
  * They need an account with that service, and stop working if it closes. Remotion's hosted MCP server shut down on 26 October 2026.

### ultrafast renders the frames

  * It draws every frame on your GPU: 3D, simulations, shaders, motion type and footage, in one document.
  * Frames and contact sheets come back as images the agent can look at, before anyone watches the film.
  * `ultrafast_review` reads every frame and names the node, the time and a fix for each problem it finds.
  * A video is a JSON document, so a change edits the nodes it touches and leaves the rest as they were.
  * It runs on your machine with no account, under Apache-2.0 or MIT.

Remotion's MCP page: [remotion.dev/docs/ai/mcp](<https://www.remotion.dev/docs/ai/mcp>), read on 21 November 2026. Remotion is a trademark of its owner. More on how ultrafast compares: [Compare](<https://ultrafast.mov/compare/>).

## Limits.

What to know before you connect it. Checked 22 November 2026.

### What it needs, and what it doesn't do yet

  * A GPU: a Mac with Apple silicon, or a Linux x86_64 machine with a Vulkan GPU.
  * No GPU? The Docker image (`ghcr.io/ultrafastmov/ultrafast`) renders on the CPU through Mesa's software Vulkan driver: frames in under a second, and a 6-second 1080×1920 export in about 17 seconds on 4 cores of a fast desktop CPU. Heavy 3D or particle work is much slower. On Linux, `mesa-vulkan-drivers` gives the other installs the same CPU path.
  * No prebuilt Windows or Intel Mac build.
  * On Linux, exports need ffmpeg; `ultrafast_voiceover` needs espeak-ng and `ultrafast_ocr` needs Tesseract.
  * The remote server at `/mcp` takes one API key as a bearer token. There is no OAuth sign-in on it.
  * OAuth sign-in and hosted rendering come with ultrafast Cloud, and so do the Claude connector and the ChatGPT app. Cloud has a [waitlist](<https://ultrafast.mov/cloud/>).
  * Lottie import is in the CLI only (`uf import-lottie`). A document can still use a `lottie` node.

## Questions about the MCP server.

Can Claude make videos with an MCP server?

Yes. With ultrafast connected, Claude Code writes the video as a document, looks at its frames, reviews them and exports the file on your GPU. In a test with the ultrafast skill, it went from a one-line request to an exported video with 0 review findings. Add it with `claude mcp add ultrafast -- uf mcp` or the plugin. There is also a .mcpb bundle for Claude Desktop. The Claude connector comes with [ultrafast Cloud](<https://ultrafast.mov/cloud/>).

Which MCP clients does it work with?

Any client that starts a local server over stdio or connects over Streamable HTTP. Tested: Claude Code used it over stdio and HTTP, Cursor CLI listed all 20 tools, and Gemini CLI connected over stdio and HTTP. The configs for Codex and Claude Desktop are in the [MCP reference](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/mcp/>); they haven't been tested yet.

Can it edit videos I already have?

Yes, as footage in a document: cut, trim, speed-ramp, reframe, grade, key and caption clips, and put the cuts on the beat with `ultrafast_beats`. `ultrafast_decompose` turns a finished motion-graphics video into an editable document. It is not an FFmpeg wrapper: ultrafast renders every frame on the GPU.

Do I need a GPU?

A GPU is the fast path: a Mac with Apple silicon, or a Linux x86_64 machine with a Vulkan GPU. There is no prebuilt Windows or Intel Mac build. No GPU? The Docker image renders on the CPU through Mesa's software Vulkan driver: frames in under a second, and a 6-second 1080×1920 export in about 17 seconds on 4 cores of a fast desktop CPU. Heavy 3D or particle work is much slower. An agent can also connect to a server that has a GPU: `uf serve` answers MCP at `/mcp` with its API key. Hosted GPUs come with [ultrafast Cloud](<https://ultrafast.mov/cloud/>), which has a waitlist.

Is there a hosted MCP server?

Not yet. The server runs on your machine (`uf mcp`) or on your own server (`/mcp` on `uf serve`, with its API key). A hosted server with OAuth sign-in comes with [ultrafast Cloud](<https://ultrafast.mov/cloud/>). Join the waitlist for one email when it opens.

# No GPU needed. Coming soon.

The open-source engine on hosted GPUs: one API key, nothing to install. Join the waitlist for one email when it opens.

Email for the ultrafast Cloud waitlist Join the waitlist

Planned

## What Cloud adds.

None of this is open yet. The engine underneath is the one you can install today.

### One API key

The same HTTP API as `uf serve`: renders, frames, contact sheets, check and review, from the SDKs, curl or an agent.

### No GPU to run

No drivers, no ffmpeg and no machine to keep warm. Renders start on GPUs that are already running.

### The ChatGPT app

Describe a video in a chat, edit it by asking, download the file.

### The Claude connector

The same in Claude on the web, desktop and phone, added under Connectors.

### Remote MCP with sign-in

The MCP tools at one URL for any MCP client, signed in with OAuth instead of a key.

### Jobs and storage

Long renders as jobs with signed webhooks, and output written to your own S3, R2 or GCS bucket.

## Run it yourself.

``` 

Questions

## Common questions.

When does ultrafast Cloud open?

There's no date yet. Join the waitlist for one email when it opens.

What will it cost?

Prices aren't set yet. They'll be on this page before it opens. The engine stays free and open source.

Can I render on my own GPU today?

Yes. The engine, the CLI, `uf mcp` and the render service are all open source. `uf serve` or the Docker image serves the HTTP API and remote MCP from one machine with a GPU, with one API key and files on local disk. See the [HTTP API](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/api/>).

Is the open-source engine limited?

No. It's the engine Cloud will run, under Apache-2.0 or MIT. Use it commercially, at any scale, for free.

Do the ChatGPT app and the Claude connector need Cloud?

Yes. They render on ultrafast Cloud, so they open with it. Coding agents work today with `uf mcp` on your own machine.

What happens to my email?

It gets one email when Cloud opens. It isn't used for anything else or shared.

## Get on the list.

One email when ultrafast Cloud opens.

Email for the ultrafast Cloud waitlist Join the waitlist

# ultrafast vs Remotion vs HyperFrames · Comparison

> How ultrafast compares with Remotion and HyperFrames: how each renders, speed, agent tools, licence and cost per minute.

URL: https://ultrafast.mov/compare/

Compare

# No browser in the loop.

Remotion and HyperFrames lay out a web page for every frame in headless Chrome, then capture it. ultrafast draws the frame on the GPU and encodes it there.

[ultrafast vs Remotion](<https://ultrafast.mov/compare/remotion/>) [ultrafast vs HyperFrames](<https://ultrafast.mov/compare/hyperframes/>)

At a glance

## Three ways to make video from code.

| ultrafast| Remotion| HyperFrames  
---|---|---|---  
Draws each frame with| GPU kernels, Metal or Vulkan; the planner fuses nodes into one kernel per group| headless Chrome; parallel tabs render and screenshot frames| headless Chrome via Puppeteer; 1 to 24 browser workers  
You write| one JSON document; no build step| a React and TypeScript project| HTML, CSS and JS with a paused GSAP timeline or another adapter  
Output tokens for a 10 s short| about 1,234| about 1,868| about 1,680  
Published speed, 1080p| 300 frames with 6-sample motion blur in 0.34 s on one RTX 5090| an 80 s video in 15 s on Lambda, up to 200 functions| 300 frames in 9.8 s; 25 s with one costly CSS rule  
GPU| renders on it| not used by default; none on Lambda| optional, for WebGL and hardware encoding  
Agents check and review| `check` before rendering; `review` reads every frame for unreadable, clipped or too-brief text and flashing; `inspect` maps pixels to nodes| no built-in review| no built-in review  
Agent surfaces| 20 MCP tools, local and remote; skills; ChatGPT and Claude apps coming soon| 13 Agent Skills; plugins for 5 coding agents; hosted MCP shut down in October 2026| 9 skills; plugins for 6 agents; Claude connector; ChatGPT Work plugin  
Same pixels on every machine| bundled fonts, the same kernels everywhere| frames must be pure functions of the frame number| fonts and Chrome versions can shift pixels; Docker pins them  
Export| MP4 (H.264, HEVC, AV1), ProRes to 4444 XQ, transparent ProRes and WebM, GIF, PNG and EXR sequences, sound alone; any size, sharp; draft to master| H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9, AV1, ProRes, GIF, transparent video, image sequences, sound alone; `--scale`| H.264, H.265, ProRes, transparent WebM and MOV, GIF, PNG sequences, HLS, HDR10; 1080p or 4K  
3D, simulation, shaders| in the same graph: 3D with image-based light and glass, raymarching, particles, fluid, feedback, Slang shaders| Three.js through React Three Fiber, shaders| Three.js, WebGPU, WebGL shader transitions  
Licence| Apache-2.0 or MIT| source-available: free up to 3 people; companies $0.01 a render ($100/mo minimum) or $25 a seat| Apache-2.0  
Hosted rendering| your own GPU with `uf serve`; ultrafast Cloud has a [waitlist](<https://ultrafast.mov/cloud/>)| none; Lambda runs in your AWS account| HeyGen credits, or your own Lambda or Cloud Run

Cost

## A 10-second short.

What it takes to write and render one vertical 1080p clip, the most common thing agents make. Tokens at $20 per million output tokens.

| to write it| to render it| also needed  
---|---|---|---  
ultrafast, your GPU| about 2¢ of tokens| nothing| a Mac or a Vulkan GPU  
Remotion, company of 4+| about 4¢ of tokens| $0.01 licence fee plus Lambda compute in your AWS account| $100 a month minimum, an AWS account  
HyperFrames| about 3¢ of tokens| your own Lambda or Cloud Run compute, or HeyGen credits| Node 22, FFmpeg, a cloud account  
  
Which one

## Pick by the job.

### Choose ultrafast when

  * An agent writes the video and should see and fix it before anyone watches.
  * You render a lot: shorts at scale, one video per customer, every aspect ratio.
  * You want 3D, particles, fluid or shaders in the same document as the captions.
  * You want a permissive licence with no per-render fee.

### Choose a browser renderer when

  * Your team already builds the video's parts as React components or HTML and CSS.
  * You need an embeddable web player (Remotion) or HeyGen's avatars and voices (HyperFrames).
  * You need HDR or HLS output today.
  * You have no GPU and don't want to use a hosted service.

For more options, the page on [open-source Remotion alternatives](<https://ultrafast.mov/alternatives/remotion/>) compares eight tools, with when to choose each.

Questions

## Common questions.

Is ultrafast a Remotion alternative?

Yes. Both make video from code. Remotion renders React components in headless Chrome; ultrafast renders a JSON document on the GPU with no browser, under Apache-2.0 or MIT with no per-render fee.

Is ultrafast a HyperFrames alternative?

Yes. HyperFrames turns HTML and GSAP into video in headless Chrome. ultrafast has the same permissive licence, renders on the GPU with no browser, and gives agents tools to review their frames.

Why does a browser renderer take longer?

It lays out a web page for every frame, then captures it from the browser and hands it to an encoder. ultrafast compiles the document into GPU kernels once, draws each frame directly and encodes it on the same GPU, without copying frames back to the CPU.

Can I bring videos I already made?

Yes. `uf reconstruct` turns a finished video into an editable document draft: shots, text layers in matched fonts, backgrounds and fades. Or ask your agent to rewrite a composition as a document.

Why does an agent need fewer tokens with ultrafast?

A document only describes the video: nodes and their params. A Remotion or HyperFrames project also needs imports, components, CSS, timeline set-up and project files, and grain, a grade or captions timed to each word are code to write. In ultrafast each of those is one node. Measured on the same 10-second short: 1,234 output tokens in ultrafast, 1,680 in HyperFrames and 1,868 in Remotion (tiktoken o200k_base).

**Sources** , checked 21 November 2026: Remotion [pricing](<https://www.remotion.dev/docs/license/pricing>), [team size](<https://www.remotion.dev/docs/terms#TeamSize>), [Lambda](<https://www.remotion.dev/lambda>), [MCP](<https://www.remotion.dev/docs/ai/mcp>), [skills](<https://www.remotion.dev/docs/ai/skills>), [GPU](<https://www.remotion.dev/docs/gpu>), [flickering](<https://www.remotion.dev/docs/flickering>); HyperFrames [repository](<https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes>), [CLI](<https://hyperframes.heygen.com/packages/cli>), [performance](<https://hyperframes.heygen.com/guides/performance>), [determinism](<https://hyperframes.heygen.com/concepts/determinism>), [plugins](<https://hyperframes.heygen.com/guides/plugins>), [Lambda](<https://hyperframes.heygen.com/deploy/aws-lambda>). Product names belong to their owners.

`curl -fsSL https://ultrafast.mov/install.sh | sh` [Read the quickstart](<https://ultrafast.mov/docs/>)

# ultrafast vs Remotion · A Remotion alternative on the GPU

> Remotion renders React in headless Chrome. ultrafast renders a JSON document on the GPU: faster renders, no per-render licence fee, and tools that let agents see their work.

URL: https://ultrafast.mov/compare/remotion/

Compare

# ultrafast vs Remotion.

Remotion renders React components in headless Chrome, one screenshot per frame. ultrafast renders a JSON document on the GPU. Both make video from code; they differ in speed, licence and what an agent can see.

At a glance

## Side by side.

| ultrafast| Remotion  
---|---|---  
How a frame is made| GPU kernels compiled from the document; encoded on the same GPU with no readback| a React tree laid out in Chrome Headless Shell, screenshotted, encoded with FFmpeg  
You write| one JSON document, checked before it renders| a React and TypeScript project  
Output tokens for a 10 s short| about 1,234, measured| about 1,868, most of it web code  
Speed| 894 fps at 1080p with motion blur on one GPU; 11.6 s of 1080×1920 in about 2.2 s on one L4| an 80 s video in 15 s on Lambda across up to 200 functions; a 1-minute example in 19 s  
Licence| Apache-2.0 or MIT, for everyone| source-available; a company licence from 4 people, counting all staff  
Price to render| free on your GPU| $0.01 per render ($100/mo minimum) or $25 per seat per month, plus your AWS bill  
Hosted rendering| ultrafast Cloud is coming soon ([waitlist](<https://ultrafast.mov/cloud/>)); `uf serve` on your own GPU today| none; Lambda in your own AWS account  
For agents| 20 MCP tools (local and remote), a skill, ChatGPT and Claude apps coming soon; frames come back as images| 13 Agent Skills, plugins for 5 coding agents, Studio WebMCP; the hosted MCP closed on 26 October 2026  
Review of the result| `review` reads every frame: unreadable, clipped, overlapping or too-brief text, text under app buttons, flashing| no built-in review  
Effects| 3D with image-based light and glass, raymarching, particles, fluid and feedback sims, Slang shaders, 19 blend modes| Three.js through React Three Fiber, shaders, Lottie, motion blur  
Export| H.264, HEVC and AV1 MP4; ProRes proxy to 4444 XQ; transparent ProRes 4444 and VP9 WebM; GIF; PNG and EXR sequences; sound alone. Any size, rendered sharp, and any frame rate; four quality levels from draft to master| H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9, AV1, ProRes, GIF, transparent video, image sequences, sound alone; `--scale`; CRF and bitrate, no quality levels  
  
Speed

## One GPU instead of 200 functions.

Remotion gets its speed by splitting a video across many Lambda functions. ultrafast renders the whole video on one GPU, faster than playback, so a short is done before a cold function starts.

ultrafast, measured

1080p, 6-sample blur, RTX 5090
    894 fps
10 s hero, same GPU
    0.34 s
11.6 s of 1080×1920, one L4
    2.2 s
10 s vertical teaser, 3D
    1.68 s
16 s launch film, 3D
    4.88 s

Remotion's published figures: an 80 s video in 15 s; a 1-minute render in 19 s for $0.017 of AWS compute.

Tokens

## A third fewer tokens.

Output tokens an agent writes for a 10-second vertical short: footage, a title, three lines of detail, captions timed to each word, a grade and grain, counted with tiktoken (o200k_base) over the files each tool needs: the ultrafast document; Remotion's composition, config and CLI commands; HyperFrames' HTML and its grading command. Measured 22 November 2026.

  1. ultrafast **1,234**
  2. Remotion **1,868**

### The same title, both ways.

The pottery teaser’s title, its letters rising in one by one.

ultrafast

```
"title": {
  "op": "text",
  "params": {
    "text": "Spin something new.",
    "font": "ultrafast:display", "weight": 300, "size": 176,
    "color": "#f1e8dc", "position": [80, 380], "valign": "baseline",
    "width": 880, "line_height": 0.9, "tracking": -3,
    "stagger": 0.03,
    "glyph_opacity": { "keys": [
      { "t": 0.7, "v": [0], "ease": "in_out_sine" },
      { "t": 1.5, "v": [1] } ] },
    "glyph_offset": { "keys": [
      { "t": 0.7, "v": [0, 56],
        "ease": { "bezier": [0.16, 1, 0.3, 1] } },
      { "t": 1.8, "v": [0, 0] } ] }
  }
}
``` 

Remotion

```
import {AbsoluteFill, Easing, interpolate, useCurrentFrame,
  useVideoConfig} from 'remotion';
import {loadFont} from '@remotion/google-fonts/Fraunces';

const {fontFamily} = loadFont('normal', {weights: ['300']});
const TEXT = 'Spin something new.';
const clamp = {
  extrapolateLeft: 'clamp', extrapolateRight: 'clamp',
} as const;

export const Title: React.FC = () => {
  const frame = useCurrentFrame();
  const {fps} = useVideoConfig();
  let n = 0;
  return (
    <AbsoluteFill>
      <h1 style={{
        position: 'absolute', left: 80, top: 222, width: 880,
        margin: 0, fontFamily, fontWeight: 300, fontSize: 176,
        lineHeight: 0.9, letterSpacing: -3, color: '#f1e8dc',
      }}>
        {TEXT.split(' ').map((word, w) => (
          <span key={w} style={{display: 'inline-block'}}>
            {[...word, '\u00a0'].map((ch, c) => {
              const t = frame / fps - 0.7 - 0.03 * n++;
              const opacity = interpolate(t, [0, 0.8], [0, 1], {
                ...clamp, easing: Easing.inOut(Easing.sin),
              });
              const y = interpolate(t, [0, 1.1], [56, 0], {
                ...clamp, easing: Easing.bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1),
              });
              return (
                <span key={c} style={{
                  display: 'inline-block', opacity,
                  transform: `translateY(${y}px)`,
                }}>{ch}</span>
              );
            })}
          </span>
        ))}
      </h1>
    </AbsoluteFill>
  );
};
``` 

The rest of the gap is project files such as `Root.tsx` and `package.json`, and the effects: grain, a grade and captions timed to each word are a component each in Remotion and one node each in ultrafast.

Licence and cost

## No company licence.

Remotion is free for individuals and organisations of up to 3 people. At 4, counting everyone in the company whether they touch video or not, it needs a company licence. ultrafast is Apache-2.0 or MIT for everyone. Tokens at $20 per million output tokens.

10,000 ten-second shorts a month| to write them| to render them  
---|---|---  
ultrafast on your GPUs| about $247 in output tokens| $0 in licences  
Remotion, Automators licence| about $374 in output tokens| $100 in render fees, plus Lambda compute in your AWS account  
  
For agents

## An agent that can see what it made.

A Remotion agent writes React and renders it; a person finds out what went wrong. An ultrafast agent checks the document, looks at contact sheets, and fixes what `review` reports before you watch.

### Write

JSON with a published schema and `uf ops` for every param. No project, no build, no `node_modules`.

### Check and look

`check` before rendering; frames and contact sheets returned as images; `inspect` names the node behind a pixel.

### Review and fix

`review` reads every frame for unreadable, clipped or too-brief text and flashing. The agent edits one node and renders again in under a second.

### Choose ultrafast when

  * An agent makes the videos and should review them.
  * You render often enough that per-render fees, Lambda bills and model tokens add up.
  * You need 3D, simulation or shader work alongside captions and footage.
  * Your company has more than 3 people and wants a permissive licence.

### Choose Remotion when

  * Your video is built from React components you already have.
  * You need Remotion's embeddable web Player.
  * You want a mature React ecosystem: in development since 2020, with about 75,000 GitHub stars.

If neither fits, the roundup of [open-source Remotion alternatives](<https://ultrafast.mov/alternatives/remotion/>) covers seven more tools and when each one is the better choice.

Questions

## Common questions.

Is ultrafast free for companies?

Yes, at any size. The engine is Apache-2.0 or MIT. Remotion requires a company licence once an organisation has 4 or more people: $0.01 per render with a $100 monthly minimum, or $25 per seat per month.

Can ultrafast render my Remotion project?

Not directly: it doesn't run React. Ask your agent to rewrite the composition as an ultrafast document, or run `uf reconstruct` on a finished render to get an editable draft.

Does ultrafast need a GPU?

A GPU is the fast path: a Mac with Apple silicon or a Vulkan GPU. No GPU? The Docker image renders on the CPU through Mesa's software Vulkan driver: frames in under a second, and a 6-second 1080×1920 export in about 17 seconds on 4 cores of a fast desktop CPU. Heavy 3D or particle work is much slower. ultrafast Cloud, which renders on hosted GPUs, is coming soon ([waitlist](<https://ultrafast.mov/cloud/>)).

Does ultrafast have an embeddable web player like Remotion's?

No. ultrafast's live player is a desktop window for authoring. For the web, export an MP4.

How many tokens does an agent spend on a Remotion video?

Measured on a 10-second vertical short (footage, a title, three lines, word-timed captions, a grade and grain): 1,868 output tokens for the composition, config and CLI commands. The same short as an ultrafast document is 1,234, about a third fewer (tiktoken o200k_base).

Remotion facts from its docs, checked 21 November 2026: [pricing](<https://www.remotion.dev/docs/license/pricing>), [team size](<https://www.remotion.dev/docs/terms#TeamSize>), [Lambda](<https://www.remotion.dev/lambda>), [cost example](<https://www.remotion.dev/docs/lambda/cost-example>), [MCP](<https://www.remotion.dev/docs/ai/mcp>), [skills](<https://www.remotion.dev/docs/ai/skills>), [plugins](<https://www.remotion.dev/docs/ai/plugins>). Remotion is a trademark of its owner.
